complexes.focus: Vertical Force Absorption to Horizontal Propulsion
complexes.execution: Altitude Drop (18-inch box) + Immediate Med Ball Chest Pass to Wall
complexes.swap: Broad Jump to Med Ball Throw

manual.why: Trains absorbing vertical landing force and redirecting it immediately into horizontal power output - a general reactive-strength quality.
manual.cue: Land soft and quiet, absorb through the legs. Pass the moment you touch down, don't pause and reset.

complexes.name: Single-Leg Axial Brace & Carry
complexes.execution: Weighted Pistol Squat (3s hold, dumbbell in the free hand) + Immediate Pallof Iso-Hold at the Same Cable (15s) + Front-Rack Trap Bar Zercher Carry (20m)
complexes.swap: Bodyweight Pistol Squat (3s hold) + Band Pallof Iso-Hold at an Anchor Point (15s) + Single-Arm Dumbbell Suitcase Carry (20m)

manual.why: Trains single-leg strength under a compressive axial load, then an anti-rotation hold in the same stance before carrying - the sequence a batsman's front leg absorbs through a long innings.
manual.cue: Hold the pistol dead still for the full 3 seconds before you release into the Pallof. Chest stays tall through the carry - don't let the Zercher pull you forward.

complexes.name: Depth Drop to Rotational Scoop
complexes.execution: Depth Drop from a 30cm Box to Two-Foot Stick (2s) + Immediate Rotational Med Ball Scoop Throw to Wall
complexes.swap: Step-Down from a 30cm Box to Two-Foot Stick (2s) + Rotational Med Ball Scoop Throw to Wall

manual.why: Trains absorbing a vertical landing and redirecting it immediately into rotational output, without a load held between the two - the stimulus a batsman gets playing an attacking shot off a bounced delivery.
manual.cue: Land quiet, two feet, stick it for a count. The scoop fires the instant you're still - don't rush the stick to get to the throw faster.

complexes.name: Approach Jump to Kneeling Side Throw
complexes.execution: Approach Jump (3-5, maximal intent, stick 1s) + Immediate Half-Kneeling Med Ball Side Throw to Wall
complexes.swap: Approach Hop (3-5, bodyweight, stick 1s) + Half-Kneeling Med Ball Side Throw to Wall

manual.why: Trains the approach-and-load rhythm into a rotational throw, the same timing a server uses to convert footwork into racket speed.
manual.cue: The jump sets the rhythm, not the power - stick it for a beat. Then the throw comes from the hip turning first, arm last.

complexes.name: Single-Leg Stick to Sled Drive
complexes.execution: Single-Leg Depth Drop from a 20cm Box to Stick (2s, dead still) + Immediate Max-Intent Sled Push (10m)
complexes.swap: Single-Leg Step-Down from a 20cm Box to Stick (2s) + Band-Resisted Lateral Shuffle Push (10m)

manual.why: Trains confirming control on a single leg before committing to a max-effort horizontal drive - teaching the deceleration skill that has to come before a change of direction can be trusted at speed.
manual.cue: Land on the one leg and go dead still - really confirm it, don't rush. Only once you're still do you drive into the sled, flat out.

complexes.name: Lateral Lunge to Pallof Brace
complexes.execution: Deep Lateral Lunge to Stick (3s, bodyweight) + Immediate Step to Split-Stance Cable Pallof Press (15s)
complexes.swap: Deep Lateral Lunge to Stick (3s) + Step to Split-Stance Band Pallof Press at an Anchor Point (15s)

manual.why: Trains loading laterally and then bracing against rotation in sequence, rather than at the same time - the delay is deliberate, since a tennis athlete often has to stabilize a beat after the lateral load lands, not during it.
manual.cue: Sink into the lunge and hold it, don't rush the step. Step across clean, then brace - nothing moves at the hips once the press starts.

complexes.name: Cut Sequence to Max Stride Sprint
complexes.focus: Cutting Mechanics to Max Stride Output
complexes.execution: Illinois Agility Run (4-6 cuts) + Immediate Stride-Length Sprint (20m, maximal ground contact)
complexes.swap: Lateral Shuffle Cut (4-6) + Immediate Stride-Length Sprint (20m, maximal ground contact)

manual.why: Trains converting a sharp change-of-direction cut directly into maximal stride-length sprinting, the transition from reactive movement to flat-out court coverage.
manual.cue: Cut hard and low through the Illinois run, then open up immediately - reach for ground, don't just turn the legs over faster.

circuits.name: The Century Maker
circuits.coach_speak: Batting for 3 hours means your legs and core give out before your eyes do. This circuit builds the muscular stamina to keep your stance rock solid and your sprints fast in the 40th over.

circuits.name: Crease Scrambler EMOM
circuits.coach_speak: You have to explode, recover instantly, and brace your core for the next ball. This EMOM format trains your heart rate to drop quickly so you are composed when the bowler runs in.

circuits.name: The Tiebreaker Engine
circuits.coach_speak: In the 3rd set, oxygen is a luxury. This circuit spikes your heart rate on the SkiErg and forces your legs to produce power through the sled and bounds when completely starved of oxygen.

circuits.name: Rotational Armor EMOM
circuits.coach_speak: Your core is the bridge between your foot plant and your racket speed. If your core fatigues, you hit the net. This builds a bulletproof bridge that doesn't collapse under fatigue.

circuits.name: The Low-Stance Crucible
circuits.coach_speak: Whether you're dinking at the kitchen or returning a wide serve, you live in a low squat. We are building massive isometric endurance in your quads and glutes so your stance never breaks down.

circuits.name: Cuff & Smash Resilience
circuits.coach_speak: Swinging a racket 500 times a match shreds the rotator cuff. This circuit flushes the shoulders with blood and builds the braking capacity needed to decelerate the arm safely.

circuits.name: The Deceleration Matrix
circuits.coach_speak: You don't get hurt speeding up; you get hurt slamming the brakes. Reverse sleds and Cossack squats bulletproof your knees and adductors to handle extreme lateral stops.

circuits.name: X-Sling Power Grid
circuits.coach_speak: Power is generated in the opposite hip and transferred to the opposite shoulder. This circuit forces your brain to wire those diagonal fascial slings together under heavy metabolic stress.

circuits.name: Alactic Death Intervals
circuits.coach_speak: Racquet sports are just a series of violent 5-to-10 second car crashes. We are training your body's fastest energy system to empty the tank and completely recharge in under 45 seconds.

circuits.name: Bilateral-to-Unilateral Transfer
circuits.coach_speak: We recruit every muscle fiber with the heavy Trap Bar, then immediately force you to stabilize that power on one leg. It's exactly what happens when you leap for a high volley and land on one foot.

circuits.name: The Sled Friction Simulator
circuits.coach_speak: The sleds in Hyrox are about overcoming massive friction under fatigue. This circuit forces you to generate horizontal force, immediately pull backwards, and then flush the lactic acid on the SkiErg. The wall sit teaches your quads to suffer.

circuits.name: Grip Death & Flush
circuits.coach_speak: Station 6 is the Farmer's Carry. If your grip fails, your race is over. We are blowing up your forearms and then forcing you to pull on the rower when you have zero grip strength left. Survive this, and the race feels easy.

circuits.name: Rox Station Crucible (No-Run)
circuits.coach_speak: This is pure station simulation without the impact of the 8km run. You have to learn how to transition from heavy legs on the lunge directly into the explosive squatting of the wall ball without redlining your heart rate.

circuits.name: Posterior Chain Engine
circuits.coach_speak: The SkiErg, Rower, and Sled Pull will completely fry your back and hamstrings. This EMOM builds a bulletproof posterior chain so you don't cramp up when you have to bend over and pull the sled rope.

circuits.name: The Lactic Wall Ball Pre-Exhaust
circuits.coach_speak: You hit the wall balls at the very end of the race when your legs are dead. We are pre-exhausting your quads with sandbag squats and the bike, so you learn how to use your hips to throw the ball instead of just your knees.

circuits.name: Off-Feet VO2 Max Intervals
circuits.coach_speak: You can build a massive aerobic engine without pounding your joints on the pavement. This is high-output off-feet conditioning. Hit your target splits on every single machine without dropping pace.

circuits.name: Sandbag Lunge Resilience
circuits.coach_speak: The 100m sandbag lunge destroys unconditioned glutes. We are using isometric holds and deficit lunges to build extreme time-under-tension so you can carry that 20kg bag unbroken.

circuits.name: Burpee Broad Jump (BBJ) Explosiveness
circuits.energy_system: Hip Hinge Power & Upper Body Push
circuits.coach_speak: The BBJ station requires a massive upper body push followed by a violent hip hinge. We are isolating those two movements under fatigue so you can cover maximum distance on every jump instead of taking baby hops.

concepts.name: 10s Tap Test
concepts.what: CNS readiness test measuring rapid unweighted foot contacts.
concepts.why: Assesses central nervous system fatigue and fast-twitch readiness.
concepts.cue: Tap your feet as fast as possible for 10 seconds. We want to see how fiery your nervous system is today.

concepts.name: Broad Jump Drop-off
concepts.why: Identifies neuromuscular fatigue and force production capacity.
concepts.cue: Give me one max effort jump. If you're down more than a few inches, we're pulling back the heavy weights.

concepts.name: Subjective Wellness
concepts.why: Captures psycho-social stress and perceived recovery.
concepts.cue: Be honest on the questionnaire. Your sleep and stress levels dictate how hard we can push you today.

concepts.name: French Contrast Method
concepts.what: 4-exercise sequence combining heavy compound, plyometric, speed, and assisted plyo.
concepts.why: Maximizes rate of force development through post-activation potentiation.
concepts.cue: We're tricking your muscles into firing harder. Heavy lift first, then we fly.

concepts.name: Short-SSC (Ankle Stiffness)
concepts.why: Improves Achilles tendon elasticity and reactive strength.
concepts.cue: Stiff ankles like springs. Don't let your heels touch the ground.

concepts.name: Helical Slings (Cross-body)
concepts.what: Rotational movements connecting opposite hip and shoulder.
concepts.why: Trains the fascial slings responsible for throwing and striking power.
concepts.cue: Whip your hip and shoulder together. Power transfers across your body.

concepts.name: MAS (Maximal Aerobic Speed) 15s/15s
concepts.why: Increases aerobic capacity and VO2 max efficiently.
concepts.cue: 15 seconds on, 15 seconds off. Hit the distance marker every time.

concepts.name: Deadmill Sprints
concepts.why: High-resistance sprint training for acceleration mechanics.
concepts.cue: Drive the belt backward. Big arms, aggressive knees.

concepts.name: Lactic "Shandy"
concepts.why: Builds tolerance to blood lactate accumulation.
concepts.cue: It's going to burn. Embrace the lactic acid and keep moving.

concepts.name: Max Effort Method (Week 1)
concepts.cue: We're teaching your brain to fire every single muscle fiber at the exact same time so you generate pure power without getting bulky.

concepts.name: Repeat Effort Method (Week 2)
concepts.what: Lifting moderate loads (60-80% 1RM) for 8-12 reps to near failure.
concepts.why: Triggers structural hypertrophy, increases tendon cross-sectional area, local muscular endurance.
concepts.cue: This is armor-building week. We're thickening your tendons and muscles so they don't tear when you lunge for a ball in the 3rd set.

concepts.name: Dynamic Effort Method (Week 3)
concepts.what: Lifting sub-maximal loads (30-50% 1RM) or bodyweight at maximum possible velocity.
concepts.why: Increases the Rate of Force Development (RFD).
concepts.cue: Today isn't about how much weight you can move; it's about how fast you can move it.
